content.content:
A ref-path entry in the detail panel's Content section is drawn in the link colour role. The thing this decision colours is the entry squvoxyr presents as a visible link: where a node's content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths, the paths the section's monospaced block shows, each of which rptlovpt makes an activatable entry, are the entries this decision draws in that role (squvoxyr, qwzwpxws, rptlovpt). The colour is applied to the entry and to the text it already shows — the path itself, unchanged — so the characters a reader is told can be activated are the characters drawn in the link colour, and the panel keeps one account of the path. Only the entry is drawn in this role: the Content section as a whole, the block of paths it shows, the content type mark beside them, the section's label and the value's frame, the other sections and their values, and the block's characters that are not entries keep the presentation squvoxyr and qwzwpxws give them, and none of them takes the link colour role by this decision.

The role is the one already recorded, not a colour chosen here. oqotyplt records one colour role for the element it names, the depends_on edge — the link colour role, the value "edge" — together with the VS Code theme token that role resolves to, --vscode-textLink-foreground, and this decision spends that role, as recorded, on the ref-path entry: the entry's text is drawn in --vscode-textLink-foreground, the entry is given no colour of its own, and no literal colour value, second role, renamed role or other recorded role's token stands in its place; the role is not re-pointed, re-valued or given a panel-specific variant. Spending the role leaves the record it comes from exactly as it is: the spec's element, aspect, state and value are unchanged, the spec is not presented as recording a colour for the ref-path entry or for any element beyond the one it names, and nothing here attributes to it a commitment about this entry. What the token resolves to — the colour a theme actually paints — is the token's and the theme's, so the entry reads in the link colour each theme provides; this decision fixes which role the entry takes, not a literal colour.

The colour does not make the entry a link. That a ref-path entry is presented as a visible link, set apart from the block's non-entry characters, is squvoxyr's; this decision takes the colour that one part of the presentation is drawn in and presupposes the link rather than establishing it. Nothing here makes the entry's link presentation conditional on the colour, and nothing here supplies in the colour's place the distinction between an entry and bare text. Nor does this decision re-decide what an entry is or what activating one does: what a path entry is, its activation inputs, its outcome and what it opens are rptlovpt's, and they are neither restated, narrowed nor extended here (rptlovpt, squvoxyr).

Colouring the entry as it rests is the whole of what this decision does to it. The decision states the entry's text colour in its default state and says nothing about the entry in any other state — hover, selection, focus, disabled — leaving whether any of those alters the entry's colour, and how, to the decisions that own them; none of them is required, forbidden or implied here. The pointer cue over the entry, the treatment the entry gets on hover, the marking it carries while it has focus, which element carries the colour, and the class vocabulary that names the entry are likewise separate commitments; none of them is fixed, required, forbidden or implied here, and none is stated as a condition on the colour. Nor does this decision name an element to carry the colour, a class or selector to select the entry by, a stylesheet location, or an ordering of rules: the role is committed for the entry, and how and where that is written belong to the decisions that own them.

A path that names no file is left where squvoxyr and rptlovpt left it: squvoxyr settles nothing about how such a path is presented and this decision takes it up no further, requiring and forbidding nothing about its colour. Nothing here colours anything beyond the ref-path entries of that form — not a path mentioned inside the selected node's kind, content or rationale text, not the node's ref list, and not the canvas the renderer draws — and nothing here presents the link colour role as carrying any of the graph's structure or edges (squvoxyr, qwzwpxws).
content.rationale:
squvoxyr made the ref-path entry read as a link and then stopped short of its colour, so the entry is a link whose drawn colour is unstated: on the panel it would sit in the block's ordinary text colour and the entry's recognisability would rest entirely on the other parts of the presentation that later decisions give it, leaving unspent the single most familiar cue a reader has for something to follow. Filling exactly that gap is what this decision does, and nothing more: the colour is an appearance fact about an entry that already exists, so it adds no element to the block, no text to the path, and nothing to what activating an entry does.

The role is taken from oqotyplt rather than invented, because the viewer already draws its followable structure in that role: the dependency edge is recorded as drawn in --vscode-textLink-foreground, and a ref-path entry is the same thing to a reader — characters that lead somewhere when followed — so the panel says "followable" in the colour the canvas already says it in. Spending the recorded role keeps one meaning for that colour across the canvas and the panel, and keeps the role in one place: a colour of this decision's own, or a panel variant of the link role, would give the token two values to keep in step and end the reader's ability to rely on the colour meaning the same thing in both places. It also keeps oqotyplt's record whole. That record names one element, and this decision does not stretch it: the spec is the source of the role and its token, not a claim that the spec prescribes the entry's colour, so the entry's colour is stated here and the spec is left saying exactly what it said.

Stopping at the resting colour is what keeps the neighbouring appearance questions decidable on their own terms. The pointer cue, the hover treatment, the focus marking, the element that carries the colour and the class vocabulary are each verifiable in the styles, so each belongs to the decision that owns it; settled here they would either be restated or contradicted by those decisions, and this one would have decided an entry's whole presentation while deciding its colour. Bounding the commitment to the entry's default state leaves hover, selection, focus and disabled open in both directions — neither required nor forbidden — so a decision that turns out to be about one of them still has something to say. Bounding it to the entry keeps the block, the type mark, the section and the frame out of it, and the paths unchanged, so qwzwpxws's value and squvoxyr's link look are taken as given rather than re-decided.

Decidability follows from the two things this decision does fix: which entry, and which role into which token. A reviewer can name the refuting observation without inventing a rule — a ref-path entry drawn in a colour the recorded role does not resolve to, the role landed on the block, the type mark or the section instead of on the entry, or the colour presented as the thing that makes the entry a link, with squvoxyr's distinction between entry and bare text made to depend on it. Each is visible in the drawing and refutable by reading the recorded role, which is what makes the commitment a settled one rather than a description of something the panel might do.
